content:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Smart-routing anomaly: continuous failover loop detected across regions (us-east <-> us-west <-> eu). High error ratio and token latency spikes. Incident created: INC-1809876543.

pagerduty-bot: Paging @kai (primary on-call). Escalation rule: 3m -> 10m.

kai: on-call here. I'm seeing churn in the region registry: endpoints for eu-prod removed then re-registered within seconds. Router metrics show failover_count spiking.

sara: initial customer impact from logs: ~8 customers with increased 5xxs, mostly those pinned to redwood-gpt variants across regions. CS looped in.

ops-bot: recent change: routing-policy "smart-global-v5" promoted to 100% at 03:12Z (author: leo).

leo: that was an automated rollout from canary; I only promoted after tests green. didn't see regressions in canary.

kai: can we get the policy config? pulling it now.

kai: config excerpt:
```yaml
policy: smart-global-v5
prefer_local: true
failover_cooldown: 10s
healthcheck:
  path: /livez
  interval: 4s
  timeout: 1s
  required_successes: 1
  required_failures: 2
```

anita: those probe values are too tight for inter-region links. 1s timeout + 4s interval = noisy on aws peering. Might be flipping nodes quickly.

matt: timeline: alerts started at 03:15Z, router_error_rate peaked 03:18Z. Right after promotion.

kai: quick mitigation options: A) pause smart-global-v5 rollout and revert to previous policy B) increase healthcheck timeouts/failures C) add region-sticky cooldown on failover D) pin model variant in eu to earlier stable build. recommend doing A+B immediately.

infra-bot: executed: pause rollout smart-global-v5 by @kai at 03:22Z. Previous policy "smart-global-v4" reinstated.

leo: ack. rolling back was expected if instability observed.

anita: applying temp healthcheck change to eu and us-west: interval -> 15s, timeout -> 3s, required_failures -> 4. Also set failover_cooldown -> 120s.

kai: applying via control-plane API:
```bash
curl -X POST "https://control.redwood/api/v1/routing/policies/smart-global-v4/override" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -d '{"region":"eu","healthcheck":{"interval":"15s","timeout":"3s","required_failures":4},"failover_cooldown":"120s"}'
```

infra-bot: override applied in eu and us-west at 03:24:30Z.

matt: also noticed model-variant mismatch logs during failover: some requests after failover referenced redwood-gpt-quant while new nodes served redwood-gpt-int8 -> caused 400s from the request-normalizer. Could make errors look worse.

kai: good catch. I'll pin eu to redwood-gpt-stable-1 for now and flush variant caches.

kai: cache flush command executed on eu pool:
```bash
kubectl exec -n redwood eu-router-0 -- redis-cli DEL variant_cache:eu
```

leo: after these changes, error rate dropped ~60% in the 10m after the override. latency 95p improved ~40% but not back to baseline.

jules (via DM to sara): CS reporting one enterprise tenant saw sustained A/B test divergence due to variant mismatch. they want timeline and rollback options.

sara: noted. drafting customer-facing message; will include what we changed and ETA for full stability.

kai: restarting eu ingress pods to ensure probe state reset. restart started 03:30Z, completed 03:34Z.

infra-bot: noticed a secondary issue: VPN peering packet drops between eu <-> us-west for short bursts. network team alerted.

anita: that explains short windows of failed healthchecks. network blips + aggressive probes = loop. network team needs to increase BGP hold timers or investigate packet loss cause.

matt: handoff to night SRE @matt (me) at 04:00Z. I'll keep incident open for 4h and monitor. escalation if router_error_rate > 3% for 15m.

pagerduty-bot: Acknowledged handoff to @matt. Next on-call: @sara in 6h.

kai: note for postmortem: root cause likely a combination of (1) rollout of smart-global-v5 with tighter health probes, (2) transient inter-region packet loss, (3) no variant-sticky policy during rapid failovers.

anita: recommended follow-ups (to include in postmortem):
- revert rollout gating to include inter-region probed runs
- make default healthcheck less aggressive for cross-region endpoints
- implement variant-sticky header or cache syncing during failovers
- add automatic rollback trigger if failover_count spikes > threshold within window

matt: action items created in INC-1809876543: owners kai (routing changes), leo (rollout process), infra (network investigation), anita (policy tweeks).

ops-bot: incident severity downgraded to P2 at 04:25Z after stabilization metrics held for 20m.

matt: leaving a note: customers partially impacted, no data loss, majority of errors were 502/504 and 400s from variant mismatch. CS to follow-up with affected tenants.

oncall-bot: Reminder: create postmortem with timeline, RCA, and mitigations. auto-schedule 48h review meeting.

kai: one final thing: saved snapshot of router logs and healthcheck traces to /ops/incidents/1809876543/logs.tar.gz for postmortem.

sara: thanks everyone. closing active page but keeping incident ticket open for postmortem and rollout policy updates. :white_check_mark:
